title: Redwood - Rate limits & multi-tenant controls demo - Acme Corp
summary: AE+SE walkthrough of Redwood Console and API focused on rate limiting, quotas, and org/project key model for multi-tenant isolation. Covered per-project quotas, soft vs hard limits, burst capacity, and audit/logging requirements. Agreed to run a pilot with benchmarks; Redwood to send security docs and pricing.
topics: Rate limiting policies (RPS, token quotas, daily limits)
Quotas vs rate limits; soft/hard behavior
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + security pack and rate-limit config doc (Lina)
Customer to share expected QPS and tenant distribution (Priya)
Schedule a 1-hour pilot kickoff for next week to run spike tests (Marcus)
Redwood to provision a demo org with project keys for Acme test environment (Lina)
Customer to confirm compliance contacts for onboarding (Sam)
action_items: Lina: Send security docs, pricing, and rate-limits reference (due: 2025-02-17)
Priya: Share expected QPS and tenant traffic profile (due: 2025-02-18)
Marcus: Prep pilot runbook and benchmark spreadsheet (due: 2025-02-18)
transcript:
[00:00] Lina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We put together a short demo to show how Redwood handles rate limits and multi-tenant controls with org/project keys. I'm Lina, AE, and Marcus, our SE, will walk through the console and API examples.
[00:18] Jared Collins: Yeah thanks. We want to understand how you isolate tenants and enforce quotas. We run a multi-tenant SaaS and need per-customer limits and detailed logging for audits.
[00:30] Marcus Chen: Great, that's exactly what we built for. Quick outline: org-level controls, project-level keys that you can attach policies to, rate-limits (per-second/per-minute), and quota enforcement per billing period. Also can do soft limits for throttling vs hard blocks.
[00:48] Priya Nair: When you say project keys, is that just an API key with a tag, or does it have separate auth scopes? We have multiple services that will call the API, and we want separate keys per tenant.
[01:05] Marcus Chen: Good question. Project keys are full API keys but scoped to a project entity. In the Console you create an Org, then projecs under it, each project gets keys. You can attach policies to projects — rate-limit policy, quota policy, RBAC roles — so keys belonging to that project inherit those policies.
[01:25] Sam Ortiz: Do you support SSO and mapping of SAML groups to roles in the console for operations? Auditors will want proof of who changed rate limits.
[01:35] Lina Park: Yes, we integrate SSO/SAML, and the audit log records config changes with user identity. We'll share the SOC 2 pack and sample audit log schema after this call.
[01:45] Marcus Chen: Let me share my screen — sorry audio glitch — okay, switching to the Redwood Console. At the top-left is the org selector, we have an 'Acme Corp' demo org. If we go to Settings -> Rate & Quotas — you'll see existing policies.
[02:10] [screen noise] Marcus Chen: Here's a policy called 'tenant-standard'. You can see it has rules: 50 rps, 3000 requests per minute, and a monthly token quota of 1,000,000 generation tokens. There's also route-level overrides, so embeddings route can have a separate quota.
[02:35] Priya Nair: Route-level overrides are important, we do lots of embeddings spikes. Can you isolate embeddings quota per project independently?
[02:45] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. Policies are rule sets that map by route type (completions, chat, embeddings). You can also scope by model family. So if a tenant is on a cheaper embedding-only plan, you can apply a policy that only allows embeddings and caps tokens.
[03:00] Jared Collins: How does the system handle bursts during onboarding? We often see big spikes for new customers. We need short bursts to be allowed but blocked if sustained.
[03:12] Marcus Chen: We support burst windows: a short-term burst allowance above the steady-state RPS. You can configure token bucket parameters — burst size and refill rate. We also support soft limits that begin returning 429 with Retry-After and a soft-throttle mode that returns a queued response or graceful fallback to a lower-rate model.
[03:30] Ana Ruiz: And if a tenant exceeds their monthly quota, do you cut them off immediately or notify first?
[03:38] Marcus Chen: You configure behavior per policy: hard cut (block), soft overage (continue and bill overage), or notify-only. Many customers prefer a tiered behavior: soft notify at 80%, hard block at 100%. We also emit audit events and usage logs to your S3/Log Archive.
[03:58] Sam Ortiz: Is the usage log sufficient for PCI/regulated SOC audits? We need immutable records, retention policies, and encryption.
[04:06] Lina Park: We support encrypted log exports, retention config, and key management options with customer-managed KMS. We'll include the compliance details in the security pack we send.
[04:20] [05:00] Marcus Chen: Switching to the API side — example call: Authorization: Bearer <project_key>. The key is tied to project ID, not org API key, so it cannot affect other projects. For extra isolation you can also enable VPC endpoints for Private deployments so traffic never leaves your network.
[05:35] Priya Nair: If we use Dedicated vs Hosted, how different are the rate limiting controls? We're considering dedicated capacity for predictable latency.
[05:45] Lina Park: Controls are consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Policies are applied at the control plane level. On Dedicated you can pin capacity and combine that with stricter quotas. The enforcement is local to the serving tier but managed through the same Console so your ops experience is consistent.
[06:05] Jared Collins: We already use an API gateway for some of our internal services — how does Redwood integrate? Can we layer Redwood rate limits on top of our gateway, or do you recommend letting Redwood be the single source?
[06:18] Marcus Chen: You can layer them. Typical architectures we see: control-plane policies in Redwood for tenant isolation and billing, and a gateway for coarse-grained filtering and WAF. Redwood's per-tenant limits are useful because they tie directly to billing and tenant-level auditing.
[06:35] [07:00] Marcus Chen: Back to the Console: here's how you create a new policy. Click New Policy, choose Scope: Project, set rules: 20 rps, 1200 rpm, monthly tokens 200k. You can set enforcement mode: Soft or Hard, and add conditions like 'if route == embeddings then tokens = 50k'. Save and then assign to Project -> Acme-Test.
[07:30] Priya Nair: Can policies be updated programmatically? We want to automate tenant upgrades.
[07:38] Marcus Chen: Yes, there's an Admin API for policy CRUD and assignment. We also support webhooks on quota events (80% threshold, exceeded, etc.) so your provisioning automation can react.
[07:58] Ana Ruiz: What's the normal delay between policy change and enforcement? We need near-immediate changes for emergency blocks.
[08:05] Marcus Chen: Changes propagate within seconds; most config changes are consistent within ~5s in the control plane, and enforcement nodes pick up the new policy quickly. For Dedicated/private we can tune control plane sync intervals if you need faster propagation.
[08:20] Jared Collins: Let's talk about org-level billing and per-project usage. We need to bill tenants individually based on usage.
[08:30] Lina Park: You get per-project usage breakdowns: tokens, requests, latency percentiles. You can export granular CSVs or push to BigQuery/S3. We also support tagging and custom dimensions to integrate into your billing pipeline.
[08:48] Sam Ortiz: Are there limits on the number of projects per org? We'll have thousands of tenants.
[08:55] Marcus Chen: No hard limit — we've supported customers with tens of thousands of projects. We recommend grouping very small tenants under aggregate projects if you need cost savings, but the platform handles many projects fine.
[09:10] [09:30] Marcus Chen: Demoing the API logs tab — here's a tenant's recent 429s. You can click into a 429 event and see the policy that triggered it, the project key, and a suggested remediation (increase quota, reduce model size, enable batching). We also surface Optimize suggestions where our system suggests batch size or quantization settings to reduce token usage.
[09:55] Priya Nair: About Optimize — can that automatically recommend different model profiles per tenant? We have premium customers who need bigger models and others on cheaper ones.
[10:05] Marcus Chen: Yes, Optimize can recommend model family and quantization per workload. You can take recommendations manually or run an automated rollout: canary to 5% of traffic then ramp. You can also tie those rollouts to cost budget policies so high-cost models flag for review.
[10:28] Jared Collins: For spike tests, can Redwood simulate high-QPS from multiple project keys? We want to replicate 1k concurrent tenants spiking.
[10:38] Marcus Chen: For pilots we can provision a test tenant cluster and provide a stress harness. We also provide a benchmark spreadsheet to capture expected QPS distribution; we'll run a controlled spike test and share results.
[10:55] Lina Park: Quick note — we'll need your tenant distribution (90/9/1 rule or other) and peak vs median QPS to size Dedicated. Priya, that was on the action items.
[11:05] Ana Ruiz: One more security question: do project keys rotate automatically or need manual rotation? We have policy that keys rotate monthly.
[11:13] Marcus Chen: We support automatic key rotation and short-lived credentials. There's also support for issuing ephemeral tokens via an identity broker if you want to minimize long-lived key use.
[11:25] Sam Ortiz: And RBAC — can we restrict who in our org can change rate-limit policies? Only ops team should.
[11:32] Lina Park: Yes RBAC is first-class: roles like Admin, Billing, Policy-Editor, Viewer. You can map SAML groups to roles so only the policy editor group can change rate limits. All changes are audited.
[11:45] [12:00] Marcus Chen: I'm going to show the webhook events now — here's a sample payload for quota.exceeded. It includes project_id, timestamp, metric, threshold, current_value. You can hook that into your billing service to trigger overage charges.
[12:20] Priya Nair: Is there a timeline for retention? We need raw request logs for 13 months.
[12:28] Lina Park: We support configurable retention up to 24 months for enterprise; long-term retention uses your storage (S3) for immutability.
[12:40] Jared Collins: Cost: if we put per-project quotas and hundreds of projects, do we pay per project? How is pricing modeled?
[12:48] Lina Park: Pricing is usage-based at the org level for Hosted. We don't charge per project; projects are logical. For Dedicated there's reserved capacity pricing plus overage rules. We'll include a pricing sheet with examples for small, medium, and large tenant counts.
[13:05] Ana Ruiz: We need an example of policy YAML or config to feed into our infra-as-code.
[13:12] Marcus Chen: Sure — I'll paste a sample policy in the follow-up mail, and the Admin API supports applying policies via JSON/YAML.
[13:25] [13:45] Marcus Chen: OK, quick recap: Redwood provides org/project keys, policy-based rate limits and quotas, soft/hard enforcement, burst controls, route-specific quotas, RBAC/SSO and audit logs, and integration points (webhooks, exports, Admin API).
[14:00] Priya Nair: Thanks, that's helpful. Next step for us is to get the security docs and share traffic profiles.
[14:10] Lina Park: Great. We'll send the SOC2 pack, sample audit logs, pricing, and a benchmark runbook. Marcus will set up the pilot environment and stress harness.
[14:20] Jared Collins: Sounds good. One logistical note: prefer the pilot next Wednesday 2/19 if possible.
[14:28] Lina Park: We'll propose Wed 2/19 at 10am PT, Lina will follow up.
[14:35] Sam Ortiz: Thanks everyone. That addresses most of our concerns.
[14:40] Lina Park: Alright we'll share the docs and action items. Thanks all.
[14:45] [call ends]
